# Performance History

What each performance change did to speed, memory and package size, with the numbers from the pull request that made it. The page is a log, not a promise: a number is only here when the pull request or a report of the project states it, and it is copied as measured. Each line reads `before → after (change) symbol`, with the change in percent after the number: 📈 is better, 📉 is worse and ➖ is the same (within the run-to-run noise, about 3% or less). Percentages were computed from the quoted numbers (the means of the quoted runs where a pull request gives several), so they can differ by a point or two from what the pull request says in words. Last updated 2026-10-27.

## How to read the numbers

Numbers from different machines, resolutions, object counts or builds are **not comparable**. Compare only the before and after of one row.

| Term | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| Real GPU system | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D (large L3 cache, which hides cache misses), NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER (driver 617.42; the machine also has an AMD integrated GPU, which the benchmarks do not use), 64 GB RAM, Windows 11 Pro 24H2, Vulkan, Release builds. Hardware read from the machine on 2026-10-27. Frame times in the 3D and Stranded II rows are milliseconds per frame. |
| llvmpipe | The software Vulkan rasterizer of a cloud container. Values marked * were read from a current cloud container of the same kind (Intel Xeon, 4 vCPUs, 15 GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.18); the pull requests do not state them, so the container of an older run may have differed. Most of the frame is the CPU drawing pixels, so changes to draw calls barely show in the time. With a tiny window (64x36) it measures the CPU side instead, which is why it is used for the million-object runs. |
| Fly-through | `benchmarks/flythrough.bb`: a scripted camera through a field of up to a million entities of 16 kinds, 640x360 (see [benchmarks/README.adoc](https://github.com/Xaymar/BlitzLLVM/blob/root/benchmarks/README.adoc)). |
| Stranded II | `tools/benchmark_stranded2.py`: a walk through a map of the game, 1280x720, 3000 frames, no vsync. |
| Noise | Run-to-run noise on the real GPU system is 2-4% for the fly-through and about 0.1 ms for Stranded II. A change inside that is not a result. |

Status of a pull request is **merged**, **open** (still a draft or under review) or **closed** (not merged).

The fly-through "base" is not the same build in every row (each pull request rebased onto the current `root`), so the 1M numbers of different rows must not be chained. For orientation only: the 1M frame time on the Ryzen 7 9800X3D / RTX 4080 SUPER system was 314 ms in the first run of #142 and 165.5 ms in the base of #190, with #156, #158, #173 and other changes merged in between. Those are different runs, so the per-pull-request rows above are the ones that isolate a change.

## Not measured yet

- [#86](https://github.com/Xaymar/BlitzLLVM/pull/86) (`-O3` and fast-math) and [#150](https://github.com/Xaymar/BlitzLLVM/pull/150) (VMA) have no before and after numbers.
- [#84](https://github.com/Xaymar/BlitzLLVM/pull/84) was measured only on llvmpipe, where the GPU wait hides draw-call savings. Real GPU numbers for the draw counts of that change do not exist.
- [#193](https://github.com/Xaymar/BlitzLLVM/pull/193) waits for real GPU numbers.
- The effect of `--enable-small` on movie decode speed ([#162](https://github.com/Xaymar/BlitzLLVM/pull/162)).
